findings.reason: the case as written is unsatisfiable under the section's own rule, so the worker either widens the rule to compare the node name before the parameter bracket (the real fix, and the case that would have caught the parametrised form of the §1 refusal) or drops the case and ships a rule that still refuses a bare name against a parametrised head id one test name at a time.
findings.text: §2's fourth case requires "A bare base name matching two parametrised head ids covers both, so a head failing only those two is admitted", but the deliverable's matching rule admits a bare name only when the head id's final `::` part equals it with parameters included, so a bare `test_charge` can never equal `tests/x.py::test_charge[1]` and `tests/x.py::test_charge[2]`; the case is satisfiable only by two ids in different files that happen to share one identical parametrised final part, which is not what "two parametrised head ids" describes

findings.reason: the worker would remove or duplicate the existing refusal text; the plan must scope the id list to the measured case where uncovered ids exist and keep the unmeasured case's arm-completion explanation, which also means naming the caller and the richer return the id list needs.
findings.text: §2 says the refusal lists the uncovered head failure ids whenever "the admission still fails", but `_zero_added_against_a_red_base` returns `False` for reasons that carry no uncovered set to list, and the caller `_require_verdict_matches_exit_status` (which owns the "two contradictory readings" sentence at line 1294 and the withheld-arm clause at 1281-1289) cannot tell them apart from a boolean; as written, a missing arm, an arm without `completed: true`, a green baseline, or an unreadable head log would have its explanatory clause replaced by an empty id list

findings.reason: a coordinator following the followup dispatches §2 and §4 concurrently into one file and into a scope the declared dependency forbids, producing exactly the lost work the exclusive-write-scope rule exists to prevent.
findings.text: the followup "Build §2 to §4" states "The three sections write disjoint files and can run together", but §2 and §4 both declare `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` as a write path, `plan-section-depends-on` makes §4 depend on §2, and s3's descope leaves two sections rather than three
